question: When white light is incident on a glass prism, it undergoes dispersion. This phenomenon is due to ________.

options.text: refractive index of the glass being different for different colours
refractive index of the glass being the same for different colours

solution:
The correct answer is __**refractive index of the glass being different for different colours**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The phenomenon of dispersion occurs when white light is split into its constituent colours.
 
• This happens because the refractive index of the glass prism is different for different wavelengths (colours) of light.
 
• Shorter wavelengths (blue/violet light) are refracted more than longer wavelengths (red light).
 
• As a result, each colour in the white light spectrum is bent by a different amount, creating a spectrum.
 
• Dispersion is a key principle in the formation of rainbows and the use of prisms in spectroscopy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Interference of Light**

 
 
• Interference is the phenomenon where two waves superpose to form a resultant wave of greater or lesser amplitude.
 
• It is commonly observed in thin films and other wave-related experiments.
 
 
 
• **Diffraction of Light**
 
 
• Diffraction occurs when light waves bend around obstacles or pass through narrow openings, causing the waves to spread out.
 
• This phenomenon is significant in understanding wave behavior and is observed in various optical instruments.
 
 
 
• **Refraction**
 
 
• Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another with a different refractive index.
 
• This principle is essential in the design of lenses and other optical devices.
